title: Meridian
blurb: A burning apartment block, a black-market arms auction, and a masked mastermind threatening to black out the whole city.

chapters.title: Ashfall Heights
opening: Midnight, Meridian City. The Ashfall Heights apartment block is burning on the eleventh floor, and the fire department's radios have gone dead the moment they got within two blocks — swallowed by a low electronic hum nobody can place. Tenants are pouring into the street. Somewhere above, a window shatters and a shape moves against the flame that isn't smoke.
gmInstructions: SETTING: A burning apartment building, Ashfall Heights, in Meridian City. A jamming signal is killing radios and phones within two blocks — this is a clue that something technological, not natural, is involved (a hidden device planted by the "Cinder Syndicate," a black-market group that deals in stolen tech and controlled arson-for-hire, though the player should NOT be told this name yet).

GOALS FOR THIS CHAPTER: The player should (1) help evacuate/rescue at least some civilians in a way that reflects their powers and stats, and (2) discover, through investigation or coincidence, a small scorched device (a signal jammer) hidden near the fire's origin point — a clue that this was arson, not accident.

GM GUIDANCE: Adjudicate the player's stated plan honestly using their Strength/Agility/Intellect/Willpower and stated powers — reward clever, in-character plans, and let poor plans have real but survivable complications (smoke inhalation, a collapsing floor, a rescued civilian panicking). Do not railroad; if the player wants to try something unconventional, let them, and narrate a fair outcome. Introduce a moment of genuine tension (a trapped child, an elderly resident who won't leave without a pet, a support beam giving way) to make the choices matter. Once civilians are safe AND the device has been found or clearly implied to be found, the chapter is complete. If finding the device happens to surface a NEW person still in danger (someone pounding on a locked door, trapped behind debris, etc.), that person must actually be freed and safe before the chapter can end — do not close the chapter on a beat that leaves anyone confirmed still trapped or in danger.
TONE: Pulpy, cinematic, a little wry, but treat danger and civilians with real weight.
chapters.imagePrompt: Night in a city: an apartment tower with flames blazing from the windows of its eleventh floor, thick smoke, tenants running out into the street in nightclothes, fire trucks parked at the end of the block, orange firelight on wet pavement.

chapters.title: The Broker's Ledger
opening: The device from Ashfall Heights bears a maker's mark: a stylized ember inside a broken ring.

It takes one phone call to put a name to it. Marlow Pike, a nervous fence who has traded in stolen goods along the docks for twenty years, goes quiet when you describe the mark, then talks fast. It belongs to the Cinder Syndicate, a crew that has been burning down buildings across Meridian City for a client no one will name. Tonight they're auctioning off "one more job" in the old grain exchange on the docks, and Pike wants nothing more to do with you once he's told you.
The auction starts at midnight. How do you get inside?
gmInstructions: SETTING: The player is investigating the Cinder Syndicate, tracked from the device found in Chapter One, culminating in infiltrating a black-market auction at an old grain exchange on the docks where the Syndicate is selling information about their next arson target to the highest bidder.

GOALS FOR THIS CHAPTER: The player must (1) get into the auction (via stealth, disguise, force, guile, or their own invented method — honor their approach), and (2) learn the identity or location of the Syndicate's leader, a figure known as "Warden Ash," and their next target: the Meridian City power authority's central relay tower.

GM GUIDANCE: Populate the scene with a handful of memorable, morally-grey NPCs (a nervous fence, a rival buyer, corrupt security). The player's tip came from Marlow Pike, a nervous dockside fence; treat him as established (he may be seen at the auction, sweating and avoiding eye contact). Let the player's stats and powers meaningfully shape how the infiltration goes — Agility/Intellect heavy characters should find stealth/deception easier, Strength/Willpower heavy characters may prefer confrontation, and either can work. If they're detected, escalate to a tense chase or standoff rather than an instant failure. Gently steer discovery of Warden Ash and the relay tower target even if the player's specific method fails, via an alternate clue (a dropped ledger, an overheard name, a captured henchman) — don't let a single bad roll dead-end the story. Chapter is complete once the player knows the Syndicate's leader is called Warden Ash and that the target is the relay tower.
TONE: Noir-tinged heist energy — tension, banter, a sense that everyone here has an angle.
chapters.imagePrompt: Interior of an old dockside grain exchange at night: tall rusted silos, a catwalk, a few shadowy figures in dark jackets gathered around a table under a single hanging work lamp, a small metal device with an ember-inside-a-broken-ring mark on the table.

chapters.title: Meridian Skyline Showdown
opening: The central relay tower rises over Meridian City like a lit match. At its base, Cinder Syndicate crews are wiring the substation to blow — not to destroy it, you realize with a chill, but to black out the entire city grid at once, covering something far bigger than arson. Atop the scaffolding, a figure in a cracked ceramic mask watches you arrive: Warden Ash.
"You put out one fire," the voice through the mask says, almost admiring. "Let's see how you do with the whole city."
This is it. How do you move?
gmInstructions: SETTING: Final confrontation at Meridian City's central relay tower. Warden Ash, the Cinder Syndicate's masked leader, intends to trigger a citywide blackout as cover for a much larger heist elsewhere in the city (leave the "larger heist" vague/ominous — a hook for a sequel, not something to resolve here). Ash has a small crew of armed lieutenants and remote-detonation charges on the substation.

GOALS FOR THIS CHAPTER: The player must (1) confront and overcome Warden Ash (physically, tactically, or through clever use of their powers/stats — combat is not required to "win," clever de-escalation or outmaneuvering counts), and (2) disarm or otherwise neutralize the charges before the blackout is triggered, OR make a compelling in-fiction case for an alternate resolution (e.g., convincing a lieutenant to turn, using the environment).

GM GUIDANCE: This is the climax — raise the stakes, let the hero's established stats/powers/bio pay off narratively (reference specifics from their sheet). Warden Ash should get one genuine complication or twist in response to the player's first move (reveals a hostage, triggers a partial arm sequence, taunts about the player's specific weakness) before the player can close it out, so the ending feels earned rather than instant. Once the immediate crisis (Ash dealt with, charges stopped) is resolved, deliver a satisfying wrap-up epilogue paragraph and clearly end the story.
TONE: Big, cinematic, a little triumphant, with a final beat that leaves a door open for "next time."
chapters.imagePrompt: A tall steel relay tower and power substation at night, crews in dark clothes wiring explosives to transformers at its base, a masked figure in a cracked white ceramic mask standing on scaffolding high above, city lights in the distance.
